name: Channels, DMs and group DMs as the room primitive
what: Work happens in public or private channels, one-to-one DMs and group DMs; channels are named, topical, searchable spaces that anyone with access can join or be added to.
how: Conversation types share one message model: channel IDs, DM and MPDM IDs all hash to the same real-time Channel Servers (user, team, file, huddle and channel IDs are all hashed), and the same Web API (conversations.*, chat.postMessage) and event types (message.channels, message.groups, message.im, message.mpim) cover all of them.
verevonRelevance: Verevon Space has only personal and room kinds, no DMs or group DMs and no human-only message path (v-space baseline), so the conversation primitive itself is the largest messaging gap.
notes: Group DMs between members of different orgs require everyone to share at least one Slack Connect channel (DOC Connect guide). Same primitive for humans and bots/apps (message.im is also the agent entry point). Quality 5: category-defining: one primitive spans humans, bots and agents, and it scales to millions of channels.

name: Threads with reply broadcast and a Threads view
what: Any message can start a thread; replies can optionally also be posted to the channel; a Threads view lists followed threads with unread replies on top; threads can be popped into their own window.
how: Thread identity is the parent message timestamp (thread_ts); notification rules differ by conversation type (all replies in 1:1 DMs, only started/replied/mentioned in channels and group DMs, per-thread override, per-channel 'all replies' option); AI thread summaries layer on top.
verevonRelevance: Verevon threads are model-turn containers; non-owner replies are refused and there is no thread side panel, so Slack's reply-in-thread + follow model is the reference for a shared-room thread UX.
notes: Slack's thread_ts keying is reused by agents: assistant threads are keyed by thread_ts too, so a human thread and an agent thread share one data model. Quality 5: reference implementation of threading (follow rules, broadcast, dedicated view, pop-out).

name: Formatting toolbar, markup shortcuts and composer keys
what: The composer shows a formatting toolbar (bold, italic, underline, strike, code, quote, code block, ordered and bulleted lists), supports markup typing as an alternative, and has list and newline shortcuts.
how: WYSIWYG toolbar can be hidden in favour of typed markup; Shift+Enter newline (Enter preference configurable); '1.' + space and '*' + space start lists; shortcuts for bold, italic, strike and hyperlink exist in the shortcut list.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's room composer reuses ChatMarkdown for rendering but is a prompt box; human-grade rich composition (toolbar plus markup) is table stakes for a Teams/Slack-class Space.
notes: The article does not cover mentions, emoji or link handling; those are known from other pages. Quality 4: solid and complete in the evidenced scope; no major gap seen.

name: Mentions with permission-gated broadcast scopes and user groups
what: People are mentioned with @name; @channel and @here notify a conversation's members, @everyone is restricted, and user groups act as mentionable handles synced from the IdP.
how: Role permissions decide who may use @everyone; @channel and @here are open to all roles including guests; SCIM syncs user groups (workspace-level on Business+, org-level on Enterprise) with live Active Directory group sync; mention routing feeds Activity.
verevonRelevance: Verevon @person is inserted as plain text with no mention record or notification, while @agent works; adding server-side mention records plus group handles (for example @team, @agents) would close the gap.
notes: Group handles that map to IdP groups are a strong enterprise pattern; Verevon could map org-core roles to mentionable groups. Quality 4: solid and complete in the evidenced scope; no major gap seen.

name: Emoji reactions and custom emoji
what: Members react to messages with emoji, including workspace custom emoji; custom emoji can be shared across Slack Connect partners.
how: Reactions are first-class events (reaction_added, delivered through the same Channel Server path as messages), are readable and writable through the Slack MCP server, appear in Activity, are captured by the Discovery API, and emoji add/remove are audit-log actions. Agents use reactions as lightweight feedback signals.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has no reactions or emoji in rooms; reactions are cheap, social and double as human-to-agent feedback (thumbs on an agent turn) so they matter beyond chat.
notes: Reactions double as workflow triggers (emoji-reaction trigger in Workflow Builder). Quality 5: reactions are first-class events, auditable, shareable across orgs and usable as agent feedback.

name: Edit, delete and edit-history semantics
what: Authors can edit or delete messages subject to permissions; whether edits and deletions are kept is a retention decision (admin-visible edit and delete logs on paid plans).
how: Retention settings with 'save edits' keep an edit/deletion log that the Discovery API and exports can read; 'don't save edits' removes it. Clips and files follow the same delete-permission model.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has no per-message edit or delete (whole-thread delete only for the owner); a ZDR-aware edit/delete with an optional audit log fits the Control/Model Plane retention story.
notes: Retention and edit logs are coupled: an architectural lesson for Verevon's ZDR propagation (edit history must be an explicit, policy-controlled store). Quality 4: solid and complete in the evidenced scope; no major gap seen.

name: Presence driven by OS idle time, not just app focus
what: While the user is active at the computer (even with Slack in the background) the desktop shell keeps presence 'active'; when idle or locked it stops.
how: Main process polls powerMonitor.getSystemIdleTime every 10 s; a value of 20 s or less counts as ACTIVE, otherwise IDLE; when ACTIVE and not locked it dispatches TICKLE_MESSAGE_SERVER, which is forwarded to every loaded web-app window so the web client pings the message server. Lock and suspend states feed the same store.
verevonRelevance: A desktop Verevon client (or the Rust gateway) could derive 'agent-visible human presence' from OS idle state, which lets agents defer interrupts when the owner is away.
notes: Semantics of the web client's response to the tickle are INF; the shell side is read directly. Quality 4: solid and complete in the evidenced scope; no major gap seen.
